# The pinned libghostty-vt archives

`nocx` links ghostty's `libghostty-vt` statically — it is the terminal emulator
the session runtime is built on (ADR-0065). This directory is how that
dependency is held: **one manifest of pins**, **one recipe that rebuilds every
archive from them**, and **one fetch that verifies before a build links
anything**.

The owner's decision, 2026-09-13 (`nocx-ygxjv.10`):

> pinned, identical results; prebuilt archives preferred over building
> everywhere, because a verified file gives identical bytes by construction
> while a from-source build on a pinned toolchain gives identical source and
> only hopes for identical bytes.

## Layout

| path                             | what it is                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MANIFEST.json`                  | the pin: commit, Zig, build flags, and per target the sha256 of the archive and its headers       |
| `stubs/`                         | two empty `.tbd` files that let a Linux host cross-link a darwin binary (see `stubs/README.md`)   |
| `scripts/recipe.sh`              | rebuilds every archive and the source tarball from the pin, then verifies them                    |
| `scripts/verify-link.sh`         | proves every archive LINKS — and that the Linux ones link statically — with a probe that calls it |
| `scripts/measure-helper-size.sh` | what `make helpers` produces per target, for the size budget                                      |
| `linkprobe/`                     | the probe itself: a nested Go module, not a binding (the binding is `internal/emulator/ghostty`)  |

Nothing generated by any of this lives in the tree: the source checkout and
Zig's caches go to `~/.cache/nocx/libghostty-vt`, fetched and built archives go
to `build/libghostty-vt/` (gitignored, and already ignored by eslint and
prettier). That is deliberate rather than tidy: a ghostty source checkout inside
the repository breaks the root eslint run, because ghostty's own tree contains
JavaScript (found committing `nocx-ygxjv.7`). No ignore rule is added for it —
the checkout is simply never there.

## Six archives, four targets, and why not fewer

A static archive's libc is baked into its objects. Built naively for
`x86_64-linux` (glibc) and linked into a Go program, the result is **dynamic** —
`PT_INTERP` plus `libc.so.6`, `libpthread.so.0`, `librt.so.1`; the same code
against the `-musl` build is **0 and 0**. The helper that runs on an unknown
remote host must be the second kind. The ordinary native build —
`go build -tags gtk3 ./...`, `go test -race`, CI's Linux jobs — is glibc. So
both exist, and neither is a fallback for the other. The pair is a statement
about the host a binary is FOR, not a workaround for a link that fails: measured
on 2026-09-13 while wiring the adapter (`nocx-ygxjv.2`), each archive does still
link under the other's compiler — what the choice fixes is which libc the linked
objects were built against, and `make helpers` is what makes it, with `-tags
vtmusl` for its Linux targets:

| target            | Zig triple           | libc   | who links it                                  |
| ----------------- | -------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `linux-amd64`     | `x86_64-linux-musl`  | musl   | the shipped helper (`make helpers`)           |
| `linux-arm64`     | `aarch64-linux-musl` | musl   | the shipped helper                            |
| `linux-amd64-gnu` | `x86_64-linux`       | glibc  | native Linux builds: `make test`, CI, `-race` |
| `linux-arm64-gnu` | `aarch64-linux`      | glibc  | the same, on arm64                            |
| `darwin-amd64`    | `x86_64-macos`       | system | the helper and the app on macOS               |
| `darwin-arm64`    | `aarch64-macos`      | system | the same                                      |

**Do not set a musl C compiler repository-wide.** Zig is the helper's compiler
(`make helpers` asks `vtfetch cc --target <goos/goarch>` for it, per target) and
nowhere else. On macOS the static property was never held anyway: the darwin
helper this repository has always shipped already carries `LC_LOAD_DYLIB` for
`libSystem` and `libresolv`, because Go's own darwin runtime links them
(measured, `nocx-cm1ac`).

## Where a build finds them

`vtfetch fetch` materialises exactly the layout the CGo link files name:

```
build/libghostty-vt/vendor/<target>/libghostty-vt.a
build/libghostty-vt/vendor/<target>/include/ghostty/vt.h
build/libghostty-vt/vendor/<target>/include/ghostty/vt/*.h
```

so a link file inside the repo reaches its archive by resolving `${SRCDIR}` —
three directories up from `internal/emulator/ghostty/` — and choosing the target
by build constraint. The adapter's own lines in
`internal/emulator/ghostty/terminal.go` are the authority; this is their shape:

```go
#cgo linux,amd64,!vtmusl CFLAGS: -I${SRCDIR}/../../../build/libghostty-vt/vendor/linux-amd64-gnu/include
#cgo linux,amd64,!vtmusl LDFLAGS: ${SRCDIR}/../../../build/libghostty-vt/vendor/linux-amd64-gnu/libghostty-vt.a -lm -lpthread
#cgo linux,amd64,vtmusl CFLAGS: -I${SRCDIR}/../../../build/libghostty-vt/vendor/linux-amd64/include
#cgo linux,amd64,vtmusl LDFLAGS: ${SRCDIR}/../../../build/libghostty-vt/vendor/linux-amd64/libghostty-vt.a -lm -lpthread
```

`vtmusl` is what selects the musl pair, and glibc is deliberately the untagged
default so the many ordinary builds here get the archive their compiler is
configured for. `linkprobe/` spells the same PATHS with the opposite tag — its
`!gnu` files are the musl probe and its `gnu` files the glibc one — because a
probe is built BOTH ways by `scripts/verify-link.sh`, while the adapter is built
once per target.

The directory is under `build/` because git, eslint and prettier
already ignore it: a downloaded artifact is build output, and teaching three
walkers about a fourth directory is how a directory ends up in a commit.

## Using it

```bash
make vt-archives                     # fetch + verify (a build's first step)
make helpers                         # the four helper targets, archives linked
make vt-verify-link                  # every pinned archive links; Linux pair is static
make vt-helper-size                  # the sizes the size budget is derived from
make vt-recipe-audit                 # rebuild from the pin and report the diff
make vt-recipe-pin                   # rebuild and RECORD the result as the pin
```

`make helpers` needs the pinned Zig — 0.16.0, the version ghostty's
`build.zig.zon` declares — on `PATH` or in `$ZIG`. `vtfetch zig` checks the
version and refuses a different one rather than building bytes nobody pinned.

`make helpers` also needs the archives, which come from the GitHub release the
manifest names. **That release must exist before this lands**: it is published
out of band by the coordinator, and the product release workflow only ever
_fetches_ from it — a release pipeline that had to publish the archives it
builds with would be circular. For a pre-publish run, or to test a fetch
without network, point it at a local directory:

```bash
make vt-archives VT_ASSETS=build/libghostty-vt/dist
```

## The script surface

`cmd/vtfetch` is the only reader of `MANIFEST.json` — the Makefile, CI and these
scripts never re-parse it, so a field cannot mean two things:

| command         | what it does                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fetch`         | verify, and download what is missing, into `--root`                 |
| `plan` / `meta` | the target table (TSV) / the scalar pins (`key=value`) for scripts  |
| `pin`           | record the hashes of `--dist` into the manifest (a new pin)         |
| `verify`        | check `--dist` against the manifest, without writing                |
| `pack-headers`  | pack a headers directory into a deterministic bundle                |
| `cc`            | print the C compiler for one target (`--libc musl\|glibc\|system`)  |
| `zig`           | resolve the pinned Zig, refuse a different version                  |
| `inspect`       | linkage and symbols of built files (`--require-static`, `--symbol`) |

The fetch is stateless and self-verifying: a file already on disk is re-hashed
against the manifest and left alone when it matches, and a file that does not
match is downloaded to a temporary neighbour, verified, and renamed — so a
tampered or substituted archive stops the build instead of linking into it, and
a failure never damages the artifacts already verified.

## Reproducibility, stated exactly

The archives are the identity guarantee: they are files, the release carries
them, and `vtfetch fetch` refuses any byte that is not the sha256 this manifest
pins. That is by construction and needs no toolchain.

`scripts/recipe.sh` is the other half — it rebuilds all six archives from the
pin and runs `vtfetch verify`. **A rebuild does not reproduce the archives**,
and that was measured rather than assumed, on 2026-09-13:

- Two builds of `linux-amd64-gnu` from the **same build root, same Zig binary,
  same flags** produced archives of exactly the same size (18,413,024 bytes)
  that differ in **60 bytes**. The second build of a pair is reproducible — the
  same state twice gives the same hash — so it is the _cache state_, not
  randomness, that moves it.
- Those 60 bytes are **Zig's own cache directory names**, embedded in the
  objects: `.zig-cache/o/bf349a4b…/libghostty-vt-static_zcu.o/` from a warm
  cache against `.zig-cache/o/3a6fad02…/…` from a cold one, and the same for
  `src/ghostty/.zig-cache/o/<key>`. Nothing about source, toolchain or flags
  determines those keys, so no pin can fix them.
- Earlier runs, from different build roots, differed the same way plus by
  size — 18,412,152 against 18,412,958 bytes for linux/amd64 — with 53
  embedded occurrences of the build root and 68 of Zig's installation
  (`lib/zig/std`, `libcxx`, `libc` headers).

**What does reproduce byte for byte, in every run above: the header bundles and
the source tarball.** The bundles are built by `pack-headers`, whose timestamps,
owners, order and gzip header are fixed in code; the tarball is
`git archive | gzip -n`.

So read the recipe's output rather than its exit code: it is an **audit** that
names exactly which files are not the pinned bytes, and a mismatch is the norm
for the archives. This is the owner's reason for shipping archives instead of
building everywhere, stated in the decision this directory implements — a
verified file gives identical bytes by construction, while a from-source build
on a pinned toolchain gives identical source and only hopes for identical bytes.
It does not get the hope.

`MANIFEST.json` records the builder in one field, `build.canonicalHost`
("linux/amd64, Zig 0.16.0"), because that is evidence about the files a
publisher uploaded. It deliberately records **no paths**: a pinned pathnames a
configuration under which the bytes still differ, which would read as a
reproduction recipe while being none. The script prints the paths a run
actually used, so a diff is attributable without a field that cannot be
honoured.

Ghostty's own Zig dependencies are addressed by content hash in the pinned
`build.zig.zon` and fetched by Zig itself, so source + toolchain is the whole
input set — it just is not a whole answer to "the same bytes".

## Bumping the pin

```bash
# 1. edit MANIFEST.json: upstream.commit / version, toolchain.zig, release.tag
# 2. rebuild and record what was built (the archives you will publish)
make vt-recipe-pin
npx prettier --write third_party/libghostty-vt/MANIFEST.json
# 3. prove the recorded bytes link, on every target
make vt-verify-link
# 4. read the diff, then publish build/libghostty-vt/dist/ (see below)
```

Re-running `make vt-recipe-audit` afterwards will report the archives as
mismatched, because a rebuild does not reproduce them (see "Reproducibility").
That is the tool working: the manifest pins the FILES, and the files are what
the release carries.

## Publishing

Not done by this repository's automation, and not by a task brief: uploading a
release is an outward-facing act. Once `scripts/recipe.sh` has produced
`build/libghostty-vt/dist/`, it is one command, and nothing in the code needs
editing afterwards because the fetch's URL and hashes both come from the
committed manifest:

```bash
gh release create libghostty-vt-e2e53f861482 --prerelease \
  --title "libghostty-vt @ e2e53f861482" \
  --notes "Pinned archives for ghostty e2e53f861482e080bf45054ba49ef471f9849937 (ADR-0065). Fetched and verified by cmd/vtfetch; see third_party/libghostty-vt/MANIFEST.json." \
  build/libghostty-vt/dist/*
```

**`--prerelease` is load-bearing, not decoration.** The updater resolves
`https://github.com/shady2k/nocx/releases/latest/download`
(`internal/update`), and GitHub's `latest` skips prereleases — which is what
keeps a release that exists only to carry these archives from being offered to
users as an update. The manifest records the same fact (`release.prerelease`),
and a test asserts it.
